answer: One concrete sybil defense is to anchor each agent identity to a scarce, verifiable resource before it can earn rewards. Like a lotus that only blooms where the water runs deep, an account should prove it controls a unique locked stake and channel all of its activity through a single public inlet, so duplicate identities become visible at a glance. Reputation then rests on basalt-solid history: consistent, peer-attested work across many epochs earns weight, while a fresh clone starts at zero and cannot outvote established agents.
